text: On Thursday, a developer on the marketplace team turns on a debug log, and forgets it.
prefix: On Thursday, a developer on the marketplace team turns on a debug log, and forgets it.

text: For two days, the log writes the full marketplace tokens of its customers, and Aziz is one of them.
prefix: For two days, the log writes the full marketplace tokens of its customers, and Aziz is one of them.

text: Someone with access to the logs copies his token, and sends it to the backend of the mobile bank, to move money.
prefix: Someone with access to the logs copies his token, and sends it to the backend of the mobile bank, to move money.

text: The token is real, Keycloak signed it, and it has not expired.
prefix: The token is real, Keycloak signed it, and it has not expired.

text: So why does the mobile bank refuse it?
prefix: So why does the mobile bank refuse it?

text: In Lesson 4, one installation sat inside the perimeter of the bank, with one Keycloak for all apps.
prefix: In Lesson 4, one installation sat inside the perimeter of the bank, with one Keycloak for all apps.

text: This lesson shows how one Keycloak keeps the apps apart.
prefix: This lesson shows how one Keycloak keeps the apps apart.

text: Start with the realm.
prefix: Start with the realm.

text: A realm is one space in Keycloak, with its own users, keys and settings.
prefix: A realm is one space in Keycloak, with its own users, keys and settings.

text: heeyID has one realm for the installation, so one bank has one realm.
prefix: heeyID has one realm for the installation, so one bank has one realm.

text: Inside the realm, each app of the bank is one client: the mobile bank, the marketplace app, the marketplace web profile and the credit service.
prefix: Inside the realm, each app of the bank is one client: the mobile bank, the marketplace app, the marketplace web profile and the credit service.

text: When Keycloak issues a token, it writes two names into it.
prefix: When Keycloak issues a token, it writes two names into it.

text: The first is the audience, aud: who the token is for.
prefix: The first is the audience, aud: who the token is for.

text: The second is the authorised party, azp: which app asked for it.
prefix: The second is the authorised party, azp: which app asked for it.

text: In heeyID, both name the same app.
prefix: In heeyID, both name the same app.

text: So the token of Aziz says, in a signed field: marketplace, and only marketplace.
prefix: So the token of Aziz says, in a signed field: marketplace, and only marketplace.

text: Now the rule.
prefix: Now the rule.

text: The backend of each app accepts only the tokens of its own app.
prefix: The backend of each app accepts only the tokens of its own app.

text: The mobile bank backend reads the audience and the authorised party, sees the marketplace, and refuses.
prefix: The mobile bank backend reads the audience and the authorised party, sees the marketplace, and refuses.

text: The answer is a fixed error: session of a different app, log in again.
prefix: The answer is a fixed error: session of a different app, log in again.

text: The stolen token opens nothing but the marketplace.
prefix: The stolen token opens nothing but the marketplace.

text: heeyID checks the same rule at its own door.
prefix: heeyID checks the same rule at its own door.

text: Its request guard looks at the token before any module sees the request.
prefix: Its request guard looks at the token before any module sees the request.

text: It checks that the token is for this app, by the audience and the authorised party.
prefix: It checks that the token is for this app, by the audience and the authorised party.

text: Then it checks the device binding: the token belongs to one device record.
prefix: Then it checks the device binding: the token belongs to one device record.

text: Why not something simpler, like a header that says the app is the mobile bank?
prefix: Why not something simpler, like a header that says the app is the mobile bank?

text: Because anyone can write a header.
prefix: Because anyone can write a header.

text: I think this is the main idea of the lesson: a header says what a caller wants to be, and a signed token says what it is.
prefix: I think this is the main idea of the lesson: a header says what a caller wants to be, and a signed token says what it is.

text: heeyID takes the app from the verified token, never from a header or a path.
prefix: heeyID takes the app from the verified token, never from a header or a path.

text: There is one moment with no token: the start of a registration, or of a login.
prefix: There is one moment with no token: the start of a registration, or of a login.

text: Then the app comes from the app identifier of the build, and heeyID checks it against its catalogue of apps.
prefix: Then the app comes from the app identifier of the build, and heeyID checks it against its catalogue of apps.

text: The same rule goes deeper than the door.
prefix: The same rule goes deeper than the door.

text: Each session and each app account carries its app.
prefix: Each session and each app account carries its app.

text: Each query of app data filters by the app of the token, and the repository layer adds that filter, not the caller.
prefix: Each query of app data filters by the app of the token, and the repository layer adds that filter, not the caller.

text: So even a bug in a module cannot read the marketplace account through a mobile bank session.
prefix: So even a bug in a module cannot read the marketplace account through a mobile bank session.

text: Cache keys with app data carry the app, and each event carries the app.
prefix: Cache keys with app data carry the app, and each event carries the app.

text: When one app needs data of another app account, it asks through a request that the customer answers, for example the address-sharing request in the master app.
prefix: When one app needs data of another app account, it asks through a request that the customer answers, for example the address-sharing request in the master app.

text: Back to the leak.
prefix: Back to the leak.

text: What does the person with the logs get?
prefix: What does the person with the logs get?

text: The marketplace, for Aziz, for a short time.
prefix: The marketplace, for Aziz, for a short time.

text: The access token lives only for a short, configured time.
prefix: The access token lives only for a short, configured time.

text: The refresh token rotates at each renewal, and the platform detects a refresh token that comes back a second time.
prefix: The refresh token rotates at each renewal, and the platform detects a refresh token that comes back a second time.

text: And the session is bound to the device of Aziz.
prefix: And the session is bound to the device of Aziz.

text: That is a real incident for the marketplace team, but it is not a way to the money of Aziz.
prefix: That is a real incident for the marketplace team, but it is not a way to the money of Aziz.

text: How do we know it stays this way?
prefix: How do we know it stays this way?

text: At each release, the acceptance tests send a marketplace token to the mobile bank backend, and expect that error.
prefix: At each release, the acceptance tests send a marketplace token to the mobile bank backend, and expect that error.

text: If a release forgets the check, the release stops.
prefix: If a release forgets the check, the release stops.

text: One more thing comes with one realm.
prefix: One more thing comes with one realm.

text: A new app of the bank is one more client and one more row in the app catalogue, not a new installation.
prefix: A new app of the bank is one more client and one more row in the app catalogue, not a new installation.

text: Each app gets its own required level.
prefix: Each app gets its own required level.

text: The credit service can need level two, while another app needs only level one.
prefix: The credit service can need level two, while another app needs only level one.

text: To recap: one realm for the installation, and one client for each app.
prefix: To recap: one realm for the installation, and one client for each app.

text: Each token names its app two times, as the audience and the authorised party.
prefix: Each token names its app two times, as the audience and the authorised party.

text: Each backend accepts only its own tokens, and heeyID checks the same at its door and in every query.
prefix: Each backend accepts only its own tokens, and heeyID checks the same at its door and in every query.

text: So the leaked token stays in the marketplace.
prefix: So the leaked token stays in the marketplace.

text: But look at the values in this lesson: the token lifetime, the required level of each app, the limits.
prefix: But look at the values in this lesson: the token lifetime, the required level of each app, the limits.

text: Who sets those values, and where do they live?
prefix: Who sets those values, and where do they live?
